info.title: Fiboki V2 API
info.description:
Every numeric field in every response carries a Provenance. There is no endpoint that can enable live execution.

**Authentication.** A session is an httpOnly cookie issued by `POST /api/auth/login` (`sessionCookie`). Every mutating request additionally needs the double-submit CSRF header (`csrfHeader`, equal to the readable `fiboki_csrf` cookie) and an `Origin` (or `Referer`) on the deployment's exact allow-list. `x-fiboki-auth` on each operation states the requirement: `public` (no session), `session` (any signed-in role), `operator` or `admin` (role plus CSRF plus Origin); login is `origin` (allow-listed Origin, no session) and logout `csrf`. `GET /api/stream` is `session`; it also refuses a present Origin/Referer that is not allow-listed. Nothing here reads a credential from a URL.

get.description: Measured, not asserted. See :mod:`fiboki.api.health`.

One row per worker in the worker's own ``worker_heartbeat`` table.

Read-only from the worker's SQLite store. The file's mtime is not used
unless the configured path is not a SQLite store at all, and then the row
says so (``mtime_fallback``). No heartbeat is ``never_started`` with a
``null`` age, never ``0``.

The single source of truth behind the sticky banner.

Every page reads this. V1 had 14 of 19 pages that never asked what mode
they were in, and a bot-creation dialog that said "Paper trading only" as a
literal regardless of the answer.

post.description:
Always refuses. Documented, discoverable, and audited.

An endpoint that could switch this deployment to LIVE would be a single
reviewable string away from moving real money. It does not exist, and this
handler exists so that asking gets an explanation rather than a 404 that
invites someone to add one.

get.description:
Server-computed consequences of ``POST /api/system/kill-switch/disarm``.

The canonical path, beside the switch it describes. The earlier path
``GET /api/trading/preflight/kill-switch-disarm`` serves the identical body
and is kept as an alias for one release. One implementation: this route
delegates, so the two can never disagree.

Queue depths. Reported as unavailable rather than as zero when absent.

A zero-depth queue and an unreachable orchestrator are opposite facts. V1
rendered both as "0".
Every service, worker, bot, broker, check and the incident load, one clock.
Alert rules with state and last fired, plus the alert history.
Cheap enough for every page: the server time and which sessions are open.

post.description: Record that a named human has seen this incident. Does not resolve it.
Append a note to the incident's timeline. Audited; never edits anything.

get.description:
Closed trades from every source, each labelled with its own provenance.

``provenance`` is a repeatable query parameter, so 'show me only paper' is a
filter on the data rather than a different page with different copy.
The ONE surface that answers 'what should I promote?'.

The caveats to acknowledge and the consequences of each promotion target.

The promote dialog renders this verbatim. Nothing in it is page copy, so it
changes when the configuration, the evidence or the kill switch changes.

Consequences of ``POST /api/system/kill-switch/disarm``, for its dialog.

Same shape as ``KillSwitchView.consequences`` (keyed by the choice, here the
single ``disarm``). It lives in this router only because the system router
is owned elsewhere at the time of writing; its natural home is beside
``GET /api/system/kill-switch``.

post.description: The ONE promotion route. V1 had six, with different copy and gating.

get.description:
Every limit with its utilisation, headroom and band, ordered most used first.

The workstation draws these bars and decides nothing about them; the
attention queue lists the same rows (``api/limit_board.py``).
Every paper bot, worst state first. The order IS the ranking.
Net P&L of the executing mode, attributed by strategy and by instrument.
Every strategy the lifecycle store knows about, newest state first.

get.description:
The most recent monitoring tick for this strategy.

404 when the strategy exists but has never been evaluated. That is a
different answer from "healthy", and returning an empty evaluation would be
the coercion this API exists to prevent.

post.description:
Queue an experiment. Admin-gated and audited: it consumes compute and,
through the multiple-testing count, dilutes every later claim of edge.

get.description:
Validation reports on disk, per strategy.

A strategy with no report is reported as ``available=False`` with an
explanation, never as a passing one with blank fields.
Every stored backtest run (any symbol), newest first. Read-only.

get.description:
Signals, fills, levels, regimes, indicator series, events and headlines.

The window is the last ``limit`` bars at or before ``to`` and at or after
``from``. With no bar store mounted the bar-derived sections are reported
unavailable and the journal, calendar and headline sections use
``[from, to]`` as given.
Stored runs that traded ``symbol``, newest first. Read-only.

One run's trades on ``symbol`` whose life overlaps ``[from, to]``.

``from``/``to`` are the chart's first and last bar; omitted, every trade on
the symbol is served (up to :data:`MAX_TRADES`, the latest kept).

put.description: Replace the operator's whole set for this symbol. Audited; versioned.

delete.description: Clear the operator's set (a new, empty version; the history keeps the old).

get.description: Stored reviews only. A file that claims execution is still returned as false.

Newest agent-audit rows first.

A missing ledger is absent, not an empty success. A broken hash chain
returns only the intact prefix and names the sequence where it breaks.
The handler does not write ``agent_tier.json``.
What needs a human, most urgent first. The order IS the ranking.
Equity, day and week P&L, positions, bots and research load. Server-computed.
Entities matching ``q``, best first. Only entities that exist.
The workstation's live feed. Snapshot, then deltas, then heartbeats.

acceptance_protocol.title: Acceptance Protocol
acceptance_protocol.default: One smoke call and one eval of the existing ledger do not finish the 20-run acceptance protocol.

AgentRunView.title: AgentRunView
AgentRunView.description:
One agent-audit row, newest first on the page.

``activity``, ``activity_label`` and ``acceptance_protocol`` repeat on
every row: :class:`~fiboki.api.models.Page` has no slot for a page-level
status, and a bare count would be an unlabelled number.

AttentionItem.title: AttentionItem
AttentionItem.description: One thing an operator should look at, with where to go to act on it.

BacktestRunView.title: BacktestRunView
BacktestRunView.description: One stored backtest (or walk-forward fold) run, as the ledger holds it.

BookStrip.title: BookStrip
BookStrip.description: One paper session, in its own currency. Never summed with another.

CandidateView.title: CandidateView
CandidateView.description:
A strategy proposed for promotion. ONE surface answers 'what next?'.

V1 had four competing surfaces for this question and six routes to approve,
each with different copy and different gating.

Caveat.title: Caveat
Caveat.description: A server-computed qualifier. Never written into a page.

ClockView.title: ClockView
ClockView.description: The API's clock and the market sessions, for the shell's session clocks.

CommandSummaryView.title: CommandSummaryView
CommandSummaryView.description: The money strip: the book, the fleet and the research load, all decided here.

Drawing.title: Drawing
Drawing.description: One operator annotation. Geometry and a label, nothing executable.

DrawingPoint.title: DrawingPoint
DrawingPoint.description: One anchor: a UTC instant and a price. Finite, timezone-aware.

ExcursionTable.title: ExcursionTable
ExcursionTable.description:
Per-trade result and excursions, as labelled COLUMNS (one entry per trade).

Columnar, like :class:`Series`: the provenance and the units are declared
once for the table rather than repeated on thousands of cells. ``None`` in
a column is an absent value (no stop, no excursion key), never zero.

ExecutionMode.title: ExecutionMode
ExecutionMode.description: Where an order actually goes. Deliberately ordered by increasing danger.

ExecutionModeBanner.title: ExecutionModeBanner
ExecutionModeBanner.description:
The payload behind the sticky banner.

Carries everything the banner needs to be correct without the page making a
single assumption. V1 hardcoded "Paper trading only — no live execution"
into a ``confirm()`` string, so the sentence stayed the same in every mode.

Figure.title: Figure
Figure.description:
One number, with the label that makes it interpretable.

``value`` may be ``None``. A missing number is a distinct, renderable state
and must never be coerced to zero — ``data?.x ?? 0`` in the V1 frontend is
exactly how a total backend outage rendered as a flat, healthy, idle fleet.

GateCheckView.title: GateCheckView
GateCheckView.description: One deterministic gate the worker or the ladder evaluated.

IncidentView.title: IncidentView
IncidentView.description: One deduplicated incident with its full timeline.

KillSwitchDisarmPreflightView.title: KillSwitchDisarmPreflightView
KillSwitchDisarmPreflightView.description: What disarming the kill switch would do, computed server-side.

LifecycleEvaluationView.title: LifecycleEvaluationView
LifecycleEvaluationView.description: Everything one monitoring tick concluded about one strategy.

LimitRowView.title: LimitRowView
LimitRowView.description: One limit. Every decision on it was made by the server.

OtherDrawingSet.title: OtherDrawingSet
OtherDrawingSet.description: Another operator's drawings on this symbol: shown, never editable here.

PromotePreflightView.title: PromotePreflightView
PromotePreflightView.description:
What promoting this candidate would do, computed server-side.

``consequences`` has the same shape as ``KillSwitchView.consequences``: one
list per choice, keyed by the value the POST accepts. ``caveats`` is the
de-duplicated set of realism caveats attached to the candidate's ranking
figures; the dialog renders each as a checkbox the operator must tick.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: Where a number came from. Rendered next to every figure in the UI.

ProvenanceBlock.title: ProvenanceBlock
ProvenanceBlock.description: Everything needed to reproduce, or to distrust, a stored result.

RecallMatchView.title: RecallMatchView
RecallMatchView.description: One prior experiment. The body is the relation, not the report.

Series.title: Series
Series.description: A labelled time series. The label belongs to the series, not the chart.

SourceNote.title: SourceNote
SourceNote.description: Where a payload came from, always rendered, never inferred from the URL.

StatView.title: StatView
StatView.description: A headline figure, its definition, and the gate on the same metric (if any).

StrategyStatusView.title: StrategyStatusView
StrategyStatusView.description: The queryable current state of one strategy on the ladder.

TradeRowView.title: TradeRowView
TradeRowView.description: One closed trade. ``provenance`` is a field, not a section heading.

csrfHeader.name: X-Fiboki-CSRF
csrfHeader.description: Must equal the fiboki_csrf cookie. Mutating requests also need an allow-listed Origin or Referer.
